# Captain Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to the Captain, and to whoever holds the position as acting Commanding Officer. It sits alongside [textlink="Command SOP" link="GuideCommandSOP"], which binds all command staff; this document covers what is required of the Captain alone.
The duties below are [bold]hard requirements[/bold]. They are not optional and they are not someone else's job by default.
## Get the Station Running
The Captain [bold]must[/bold] ensure the station is up and running each shift - working atmospherics and working power above all.
Where a department is short-staffed or slow to start, the Captain [bold]must[/bold] see that setup happens, whether by pressing the responsible department or by helping to set it up directly.
## Oversee Day-to-Day Operations
The Captain [bold]must[/bold] oversee the running of the station. This includes:
- Handling alien and anomalous lifeforms, and threats to the station - Ensuring every anomaly on station is contained and dealt with, whether by pressing Science or by handling it themselves when Science is absent - Keeping departments talking to one another, and resolving disputes and stalled requests between them - Keeping cargo orders moving and answering requests for funding - Ensuring crew hold the access their jobs require, and no more - Ensuring prisoners are treated fairly under [textlink="Brigging SOP" link="GuideBriggingSOP"] - Ensuring crew suit sensors are actively monitored, and that lost or missing crew are retrieved
## Command from the Bridge
Where the department responsible is staffed, these duties are discharged by [bold]communicating[/bold]. Direct them over comms, confirm the work was done, and follow up when it was not. A Captain who abandons the bridge to do a manned department's job themselves has stopped commanding the station.
Where it is not staffed, the duty does not lapse - it falls to the Captain to see it done, personally if that is what it takes. Delegation is the preferred method, not an excuse; the responsibility for the outcome stays with the Captain either way.
## Authority and Succession
The Captain holds final say on all matters not otherwise reserved by NanoTrasen. Where a departmental SOP conflicts with command procedure, the Captain rules on it.
Succession, acting-captain rules, and the appointment of acting Heads of Staff are covered in [textlink="Command Hierarchy" link="GuideCommandHierarchy"] and [textlink="Command SOP" link="GuideCommandSOP"].
An arrest of the Captain or acting Commanding Officer follows [textlink="Security SOP" link="GuideSecuritySOP"] - it needs the approval of another command member where one is present, and that member takes over as acting Commanding Officer for as long as the Captain is held.
